summary: Specifies a SIP private header, P-Refused-URI-List, used in the Open Mobile Alliance's Push to talk over Cellular system. It lets URI-list servers refuse to handle incoming URI lists that contain embedded lists, and tell the client about the embedded lists they refused. It is informational and has since been updated.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 5318 defines a SIP response header for a server that refuses a request containing a list inside another list. The response can identify the refused lists and provide their members so the controlling server can contact them directly.

subtitle: A SIP header that identifies nested URI lists a server refused to process.

tldr.problem: In OMA Push to talk over Cellular, a URI list can contain other lists, but a participating server may not be allowed to invite the nested lists' members.
tldr.mechanism: The server returns 403 Forbidden with P-Refused-URI-List entries and may link those entries to response-body parts that contain list members.
tldr.outcome: The RFC is Informational, applies to OMA PoC networks, and was updated by RFC 8217.

today: RFC 5318 is Informational and was updated by RFC 8217. Its text limits the intended use to OMA PoC networks.

sections.title: Nested Lists in a Group Invitation
sections.content:
In an ad-hoc Push to talk over Cellular group session, an originator can send an INVITE containing a list of participants. Later versions of the service also allow an entry in that list to identify another URI list, such as a pre-arranged group.

One PoC server controls the session and sends invitations. A participating server may know the members of a nested list but cannot invite them itself, so it needs a way to tell the controlling server about the refused list and its members.
sections.plainLanguage: A group invitation may contain a name that refers to another list of people. The server that knows that list may need to tell the controlling server who is on it.

sections.title: The Refusal Response
sections.content:
When a URI-list server cannot handle an incoming list that contains nested lists, it returns a 403 Forbidden response with a P-Refused-URI-List header. The header identifies one or more URIs from the request that the server could not handle.

The response may also include some or all members of those lists. The client can then send requests directly to the member URIs.
sections.plainLanguage: The server refuses the request and names the list entries it could not process. If it provides the members, the client can contact those people directly.

sections.title: Header Entries and Response Bodies
sections.content:
The header contains a comma-separated set of URI entries. An entry may include a members parameter whose value is a Content-ID URL.

A 403 response may contain body parts with the URI lists. When a header entry gives a Content-ID, a body part must carry the matching Content-ID. The format of each URI list is defined by the service.
sections.plainLanguage: A header entry can point to a matching list in the response body. The Content-ID connects the entry to the correct body part.

sections.title: Example of a Refused Group List
sections.content:
The RFC's example has a controlling PoC server send an INVITE with an individual participant and two pre-arranged group lists. The participating server replies with 403 Forbidden and a P-Refused-URI-List entry for each group list.

The response body contains a resource list for each Content-ID. The controlling server can use the disclosed members to send individual invitations.
sections.plainLanguage: The response identifies each group list it refused and links each one to a list of members. The controlling server can then send separate invitations to those members.

sections.title: Applicability and Privacy
sections.content:
The header is intended for OMA PoC networks, where one server resolves incoming URI lists and special trust relationships exist between servers. The RFC says this arrangement does not generally apply to public Internet services, and the header is optional.

A response may reveal the members of a URI list. The RFC recommends encrypting the response and disclosing list contents only to authorized clients.
sections.plainLanguage: The header is designed for trusted PoC servers, not general SIP use. Because a response may reveal group membership, servers should share list contents only with authorized clients.
